{{Elections in Wyoming}}
The '''2022 United States House of Representatives election in Wyoming''' will be held on November 8, 2022, to elect the [[United States House of Representatives|U.S. representative]] for {{ushr|WY|AL}}. The election will coincide with [[2022 United States House of Representatives elections|other elections]] to the House of Representatives, [[2022 United States Senate elections|elections]] to the [[United States Senate]], and various [[2022 United States elections|state and local elections]].

Incumbent Republican [[Liz Cheney]] was reelected with 68.6% of the vote in [[2020 United States House of Representatives election in Wyoming|2020]],<ref>{{cite web |title=Statewide Candidates Official Summary Wyoming General Election - November 3, 2020 |url=https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2020/Results/General/2020_General_Statewide_Candidates_Summary.pdf |website=Wyoming Secretary of State |access-date=November 11, 2020 |archive-date=March 27, 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210327031501/https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2020/Results/General/2020_General_Statewide_Candidates_Summary.pdf |url-status=live }}</ref> but she faced backlash from her party for her opposition to [[Donald Trump]], vocal support of [[Second impeachment of Donald Trump|Trump's second impeachment]], and vote in favor and service on the [[January 6th Committee]]. She was defeated by pro-Trump candidate [[Harriet Hageman]] in the Republican primary on August 16, 2022,<ref>{{cite web|website=Wyoming Secretary of State|author=Wyoming Secretary of State|title=Key Election Dates|url=https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2022/2022_Key_Election_Dates.pdf|access-date=August 5, 2022|archive-date=August 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817022211/https://sos.wyo.gov/Elections/Docs/2022/2022_Key_Election_Dates.pdf|url-status=live}}</ref> with a landslide 66.3% of the vote going to Hageman. Cheney's margin of defeat marked the second-worst for a House incumbent in the last 60 years, behind that of South Carolina Republican [[Bob Inglis]] in [[2010 United States House of Representatives elections in South Carolina#District 4|a 2010 primary runoff]].<ref>{{cite news|url=https://www.cnn.com/2022/08/17/politics/liz-cheney-worst-defeat-house-incumbent/index.html|title=Cheney's loss may be the second worst for a House incumbent in 60 years|publisher=CNN|last=Enten|first=Harry|date=August 17, 2022|accessdate=August 17, 2022}}</ref>

==Republican primary==
===Background===
Incumbent Liz Cheney was criticized by supporters of former president [[Donald Trump]] for [[Second impeachment of Donald Trump#House vote|her vote to impeach him]], as well as refusing to object to the [[2021 United States Electoral College vote count|certification of the Electoral College results]] in the [[2020 United States presidential election|2020 presidential election]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2021/jan/15/liz-cheney-suffers-impeachment-vote-blowback-home-/|title=Liz Cheney suffers impeachment vote blowback at home: 'Couldn't win a primary today for dog catcher'|newspaper=[[The Washington Times]]|access-date=April 1, 2021|archive-date=August 17, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220817022213/https://www.washingtontimes.com/news/2021/jan/15/liz-cheney-suffers-impeachment-vote-blowback-home-/|url-status=live}}</ref> Following her impeachment vote, Florida Congressman [[Matt Gaetz]] appeared at a rally at the [[Wyoming State Capitol]] in support of ousting Cheney, with [[Donald Trump Jr.]] also supporting it by phone in January 2021.<ref>{{Cite web|last=Reynolds|first=Nick|title=Florida Rep. Matt Gaetz coming to Wyoming as anti-Cheney effort grows|url=https://trib.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/florida-rep-matt-gaetz-coming-to-wyoming-as-anti-cheney-effort-grows/article_58ed5a93-0650-5683-b9f3-fedeb1bb6aff.html|url-status=live|access-date=2021-04-11|website=Casper Star-Tribune Online|language=en|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210125225102/https://trib.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/florida-rep-matt-gaetz-coming-to-wyoming-as-anti-cheney-effort-grows/article_58ed5a93-0650-5683-b9f3-fedeb1bb6aff.html |archive-date=January 25, 2021 }}</ref> For the same reason, the [[Wyoming Republican Party]] later voted to censure her and requested that she resign or be primaried in the next election. Later that year, it also voted 31-29 to no longer recognize Cheney as a member due to her actions to participate in the [[United States House Select Committee on the January 6 Attack|January 6 Select Committee]] shortly after being removed as Conference Chair.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.npr.org/2021/02/06/964933035/wyoming-gop-censures-liz-cheney-for-voting-to-impeach-trump|title=Wyoming GOP Censures Liz Cheney For Voting To Impeach Trump|newspaper=NPR|date=February 6, 2021|access-date=April 1, 2021|last1=Ruwitch|first1=John|last2=Sprunt|first2=Barbara|archive-date=June 20, 2022|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220620093748/https://www.npr.org/2021/02/06/964933035/wyoming-gop-censures-liz-cheney-for-voting-to-impeach-trump|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news |last=Crane |first=Emily |date=November 16, 2021 |title=Wyoming GOP won't recognize Liz Cheney as member over anti-Trump stance |work=New York Post |url=https://nypost.com/2021/11/16/liz-cheney-no-longer-recognized-as-member-of-wyoming-gop/ |access-date=March 23, 2022 |archive-date=March 24, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220324035155/https://nypost.com/2021/11/16/liz-cheney-no-longer-recognized-as-member-of-wyoming-gop/ |url-status=live }}</ref>

In February 2021, members of the [[Freedom Caucus]] attempted to have Cheney removed from her position as [[Chair of the House Republican Conference]] in response to her impeachment vote. In a [[secret ballot]], 61 members of the conference voted to remove, while 145 voted not to remove. Cheney retained her position in large part because of the support by these Republicans, including [[Minority Leader of the U.S. House of Representatives|House Minority Leader]] [[Kevin McCarthy (California politician)|Kevin McCarthy]] and [[Minority Whip of the U.S. House of Representatives|House Minority Whip]] [[Steve Scalise]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.cbsnews.com/news/liz-cheney-republican-conference-chairwoman-vote/|title=Liz Cheney survives vote to remove her from GOP leadership|website=Cbsnews.com|access-date=April 1, 2021|archive-date=April 16, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210416154445/https://www.cbsnews.com/news/liz-cheney-republican-conference-chairwoman-vote/|url-status=live}}</ref><ref name=":2">{{Cite news|last=Strauss|first=Daniel|date=May 12, 2021|title=Liz Cheney removed from House leadership over Trump criticism|language=en-GB|work=The Guardian|url=https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/may/12/liz-cheney-house-leadership-republican-caucus-vote|access-date=May 12, 2021|archive-date=May 14, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210514021835/https://www.theguardian.com/us-news/2021/may/12/liz-cheney-house-leadership-republican-caucus-vote|url-status=live}}</ref> Eventually, however, Cheney's continued criticism of Trump lost her support by more Republicans, including McCarthy and Scalise, and McCarthy was caught on a [[hot mic]] saying "I've had it with her" in reference to Cheney. On May 12, 2021, Cheney was removed from her position as conference chair by a [[voice vote]] and replaced with [[Elise Stefanik]].<ref name=":2"/>

On May 21, 2021, challenger Anthony Bouchard admitted that as a teenager he fell in love with and started dating a 14-year-old girl who he subsequently impregnated then married, Bouchard was 18 at the time. Bouchard claimed he went public with the story because he had learned that the story was being investigated by others, though the Cheney campaign denied investigating it. He compared his relationship with the unnamed girl to "the [[Romeo and Juliet]] story." The two were married but divorced three years later, and she committed suicide at age 20. Bouchard continued to raise their son after her death, though he says the two are now [[family estrangement|estranged]].<ref>{{Cite web|last=victoria.eavis@trib.com|first=Victoria Eavis 307-266-0592|title=US House candidate Bouchard says he impregnated 14-year-old when he was 18|url=https://trib.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/us-house-candidate-bouchard-says-he-impregnated-14-year-old-when-he-was-18/article_c3996062-e6ad-5027-96a9-1bcd0f832eda.html|access-date=2021-06-08|website=Casper Star-Tribune Online|language=en|archive-date=May 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521195257/https://trib.com/news/state-and-regional/govt-and-politics/us-house-candidate-bouchard-says-he-impregnated-14-year-old-when-he-was-18/article_c3996062-e6ad-5027-96a9-1bcd0f832eda.html|url-status=live}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|last=Astor|first=Maggie|date=May 21, 2021|title=A G.O.P. challenger to Liz Cheney says he impregnated a 14-year-old when he was 18.|language=en-US|work=The New York Times|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/21/us/politics/anthony-bouchard-14-year-old.html|access-date=2021-06-08|issn=0362-4331|archive-date=May 21, 2021|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20210521195150/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/05/21/us/politics/anthony-bouchard-14-year-old.html|url-status=live}}</ref>

Cheney and [[Adam Kinzinger]] were censured by the [[Republican National Committee]] at its meeting in [[Salt Lake City]] on February 4, 2022, due to "actions in their positions as members of the [[United States House Select Committee on the January 6 Attack|January 6th Select Committee]] not befitting Republican members of Congress". The Wyoming delegation to the committee also submitted a "Rule 11" letter formalizing support for challenger Harriet Hageman and allowing the RNC to spend money allocated for Wyoming's party branch on her behalf. At the same time, support of Hageman surged following the censure of Cheney.<ref>{{Cite news |date=February 4, 2022 |title=G.O.P. Declares Jan. 6 Attack 'Legitimate Political Discourse' |work=[[The New York Times]] |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/04/us/politics/republicans-jan-6-cheney-censure.html |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204192035/https://www.nytimes.com/2022/02/04/us/politics/republicans-jan-6-cheney-censure.html |archive-date=February 4, 2022}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |date=February 4, 2022 |title=RESOLUTION TO FORMALLY CENSURE LIZ CHENEY AND ADAM KINZINGER AND TO NO LONGER SUPPORT THEM AS MEMBERS OF THE REPUBLICAN PARTY |url=https://int.nyt.com/data/documenttools/rnc-censure-resolution/58226d40412e4f18/full.pdf |url-status=live |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220204184350/https://int.nyt.com/data/documenttools/rnc-censure-resolution/58226d40412e4f18/full.pdf |archive-date=February 4, 2022 |access-date=March 23, 2022 |website=New York Times}}</ref> Hageman has referred to [[Donald Trump]] as "racist and xenophobic" and also as "the weakest candidate" during the [[2016 United States presidential election|2016 presidential election]]; at the same time Hageman endorsed Cheney and called her a "proven, courageous, constitutional conservative."<ref>{{cite news |title=Harriet Hageman Goes From Anti-Trump Plotter to His Champion vs. Liz Cheney |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/27/us/politics/harriet-hageman-liz-cheney-trump.html |access-date=14 August 2022 |work=The New York Times |archive-date=August 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814065119/https://www.nytimes.com/2021/09/27/us/politics/harriet-hageman-liz-cheney-trump.html |url-status=live }}</ref><ref>{{cite news |title=Harriet Hageman once rebuked Trump and endorsed Liz Cheney. She's now challenging her with his support |url=https://edition.cnn.com/2021/09/30/politics/kfile-harriet-hageman-endorsed-cheney-2016/index.html |access-date=14 August 2022 |work=CNN |archive-date=August 14, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220814152253/https://edition.cnn.com/2021/09/30/politics/kfile-harriet-hageman-endorsed-cheney-2016/index.html |url-status=live }}</ref>

Following Cheney's defeat, she called Hageman to concede the race. However, Hageman alleged that Cheney only left 2 words: "Hi Harriet". This prompted Cheney to release the full audio recording of the call which showed that she did, in fact, concede the race. The Hageman camp asserted that a technical glitch was at fault.<ref>{{cite news|title=Cheney releases concession call audio in tit-for-tat with her primary foe|url=https://www.politico.com/news/2022/08/17/cheney-releases-concession-call-audio-to-refute-primary-opponents-claims-00052593|work=Politico|archive-date=August 18, 2022 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220818035436/https://www.politico.com/news/2022/08/17/cheney-releases-concession-call-audio-to-refute-primary-opponents-claims-00052593|url-status=live}}</ref>

===Republican Debates and forums===

[[Wyoming PBS]] has had a tradition of hosting one debate for each for the Democratic and Republican primaries for all candidates on the ballot in their respective primaries as well as one general election debate for all candidates on the ballot.
